definitions.gloss: every time; whenever; each time that
definitions.explanation: Used after a verb in dictionary form or a noun to indicate that something happens on every occasion of the stated action or event.

examples.english: Every time I see him, he's gotten fatter.

examples.japanese: この{曲|きょく}を{聞|き}くたびに{泣|な}きそうになる。
examples.english: Every time I hear this song, I feel like crying.

examples.japanese: {旅行|りょこう}に{行|い}くたびに{新|あたら}しい{発見|はっけん}がある。
examples.english: Every time I go on a trip, there's a new discovery.

examples.japanese: {母|はは}は{電話|でんわ}をかけるたびに「{体|からだ}に{気|き}をつけて」と{言|い}う。
examples.english: My mother says 'take care of yourself' every time she calls.

notes:
A common grammatical pattern meaning 'every time' or 'whenever.' It attaches to the dictionary form of a verb (Vるたびに) or to a noun (Nのたびに). It emphasizes that the result consistently occurs on each occasion.

PATTERN:
- Verb dictionary form + たびに: {見|み}るたびに (every time I see)
- Noun + のたびに: {旅行|りょこう}のたびに (every time on a trip)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {会|あ}うたびに: every time we meet
- {来|く}るたびに: every time (someone) comes
- {思|おも}い{出|だ}すたびに: every time I remember
- {見|み}るたびに: every time I see

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ごとに: every; each — emphasizes regularity or intervals, while たびに emphasizes each occasion of an action
- {度|つど}に: each time — more literary and formal than たびに
